ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the square OABC, point O is the origin, point $C(-3, 0)$, point A is on the positive y-axis, points E and F are respectively on BC and CO, with $CE=CF=2$. The graph of the linear function $y=kx+b\ (k\ne 0)$ passes through points E and F, intersecting the y-axis at point G. The graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{m}{x}\ (m\ne 0)$ through point E intersects AB at point D. Is there a point P on segment EF such that $S_{\triangle ADP}=S_{\triangle APG}$? If so, find the coordinates of point P; if not, please explain why.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Suppose there exists a point $P$ such that $S_{\triangle ADP}=S_{\triangle APG}$. In the equation $y=-x-1$, let $x=0$ to obtain $y=-1$,\\
therefore $G(0, -1)$,\\
hence $AG=4$,\\
in the equation $y=-\frac{6}{x}$, let $y=3$ to obtain $x=-2$,\\
therefore $D(-2, 3)$,\\
thus $AD=2$,\\
let $P(t, -t-1)$,\\
since $S_{\triangle ADP}=S_{\triangle APG}$,\\
it follows that $\frac{1}{2}\times 2\cdot [3-(-t-1)]=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times (-t)$,\\
solving this yields $t=-\frac{4}{3}$,\\
therefore \boxed{P\left(-\frac{4}{3}, \frac{1}{3}\right)}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is square OABC in the coordinate system, O is near the origin, OA is in the positive direction of the y-axis, OC is in the negative direction of the x-axis, AB is the upper side, and BC is the left side. There is also an inverse proportional function curve passing through E and intersecting the upper side AB at D. In the figure, P is located on line segment EF. E is on BC and CE=2, so E=(-3,2); F is on CO and CF=2, so F=(-1,0). The slope of line EF is (0-2)/[-1-(-3)]=-2/2=-1, therefore the equation of the line is y=-x-1. It intersects the y-axis at x=0, so G=(0,-1), hence AG=3-(-1)=4. The inverse proportional function y=m/x passes through E(-3,2), so m=(-3)·2=-6, and the function is y=-6/x. It intersects AB, and the equation of AB is y=3; substituting gives 3=-6/x, solving gives x=-2, so D=(-2,3), therefore AD=2. Let P=(t,-t-1) be on EF. When taking AD as the base, the height of triangle ADP is 3-(-t-1)=t+4, so S_triangle_ADP=1/2·2·[3-(-t-1)]. When taking AG as the base, the height of triangle APG is the distance from point P to the y-axis, namely -t, so S_triangle_APG=1/2·4·(-t). Set the two areas equal: 1/2·2·[3-(-t-1)] = 1/2·4·(-t), namely t+4=-2t, solving gives t=-4/3. At this time y=-t-1=4/3-1=1/3. Also, -4/3 is within the interval [-3,-1], so P is on line segment EF.
